title: Destruction of Carthage (146 BCE)
note: Siege of 149–146 BCE, six days of street fighting, ~50,000 surrendered from the Byrsa (Appian 130, Livius text); province of Africa; Punic civilization and its afterlife centred. UNESCO WHC 37 (note its brief synthesis misprints 146 AD); Pleiades 314921 coordinates. audience_note.

title: Roman sack of Epirus and enslavement of its population (167 BCE)
note: 70 cities, 150,000 people (mostly Molossians) sold, per Polybius via Plutarch Aem. 29; Antoniadis & Pliakou 2022 show many settlements survived — ancient account versus archaeology as perspectives. Centre the enslaved; one of the largest single enslavements recorded in antiquity.

title: Spartacus slave revolt (73–71 BCE)
note: Escape of 78 gladiators from Capua, campaigns across Italy, defeat by Crassus, ~6,000 crucified on the Via Appia. Needs Plutarch Crassus and Appian Civil Wars 1.116–120 opened directly; path geometry. Enslaved people's history.

title: Punic Wars (264–146 BCE)
note: Parent record for the three wars (264–241, 218–201, 149–146); children: Cannae 216, Zama 202 (19 October per WHE; calendar to check), Hannibal's Alpine crossing. Polybius Books 1–3 on LacusCurtius; Carthaginian perspective and Hannibal's Iberian base (Carthago Nova).

title: Kingdom of Numidia
note: Amazigh (Berber) kingdom of Masinissa, whose war with Carthage in 150 BCE triggered the Third Punic War; Jugurtha; annexation under Caesar. Under-recorded North African polity; Medracen and Cirta as places.
